quote: VaisHNnavs, or Maédhva Brahmans, aregreturned as numbering about 300 and as found in all sub-divisions. They are said to havecome from the Bombay Karnétak within the last hundred years.
notes: Contrast: Deshasth, Chitpāvan and Karhāḍā councils refer serious breaches to Shankaracharya of Sankeshvar, whose 'power is growing weaker day by day' (p. 60)

what_is_said: The Konkani Sonārs (10,158) are Vaiṣṇavs under Vyāsrāj Svāmī of Udupi, paying him large sums and taking the branded seals
quote: They are Vaishnavs and have as their religious Teacher Vyasrdj Svdmi, the head of the i Vaishnav monastery of Udipi in South Kanara. They pay him lai^ sums which are called garukdnike or presents to the Teacher,
notes: garukāṇike = guru-kāṇike

what_is_said: The Aksālī goldsmiths (c. 200) above the Ghats follow the head of the Vaiṣṇav maṭh at Sonda
quote: Their religious observances do not differ from those of the Aksdlis, and their religious Teacher is the head of the Vaishnav monastery at Sonda.
notes: Statement for Golak Sonārs; the Sode maṭh at Sonda

what_is_said: The Shivallis, a Havig branch, broke away about forty years earlier after a religious dispute and became Mādhvas under the Sonda maṭh
quote: They are a branch of the Havigs who separated about forty years ago in consequence of a religious dispute.
notes: p. 136-37: 'They are Madhva Vaishnavs and their spiritual guide is the head of the Sonda monastery in Sirsi.' A secession from a Smārta (Havig) guru to a Mādhva one

what_is_said: The Konkani Sasashtkārs (8,858) hold Mādhva doctrine without special reverence to Madhva's successors; one section had a caste teacher initiated by the Udupi head
quote: Konkanigs ar© Vaishnavs in religion, adopting the Madhva doctrine that Vishnu is greater than Shiv, though they do not show special respect to Madhv^harya's descendants.
notes: Footnote: formerly Smārts under a Shenvi teacher; 'had a teacher of their own caate initiated- hv the Vaisbaav head ot the Udipi mwiastery'

what_is_said: The Bārdeskārs (657) and Fedṇekārs (102) are Vaiṣṇavs under the head of the Partagāḷī maṭh in Goa
quote: Like the Sasashtkars they are Vaishnavs, reverencing the head of the Partgali monastery in Goa and employing Sasashtkdrs as family priests.
notes: Gauḍa Sārasvat Mādhva seat

what_is_said: Among the Karnāṭaka Brahmans the Vaiṣṇavs follow the celibate Tulu head of the Udupi maṭh and the Smārts the head of Śṛṅgeri; Deshasths (601) split the same way (Vaiṣṇav guide at Sira, living at Udupi)

quote: Till last year (1881) they were followers of the Lmgayat guide of Ohitaldurg in Maisur. But the pdrupatyagdr or ^napr of the Smdrt Jagadguru of Shringeri has persuaded them to acknowledge him as their Teacher
notes: Already cited in sringeri/README; the clearest case of a caste won from a Liṅgāyat seat to a Śaṅkara one

what_is_said: The Banjigs (1,082 in 1872; folded into 'Lingayats' in 1881) and other Liṅgāyats take the head of the Chitradurga maṭh as high-priest
quote: Their high-priest or Teacher is the head of the Lingdyat monastery at Chitaldurg in Maisur.
notes: Kanara also notes the Liṅgāyat chiefs of Sonda; Ulvi is the main pilgrimage centre

what_is_said: The Kāmtis (448) take as teacher the Yatyāchārī of the Śrīvaiṣṇava maṭh near Tirupati; the Bāndekar Vāṇīs (477) also follow the Śrīvaiṣṇava high priest after Liṅgāyat priests lost influence over them
quote: Their religious Tether is the Tfity4chari of the Shrivaishnava monastery at Govindrajpattan near Tirupati.
notes: Bāndekars p. 182: 'They seem to have once been Lingayats, but Lingdyat priests have now no influence over them.'

what_is_said: Liṅgāyat Vāṇī caste meetings are held in maṭhs; offenders pay fines to the town's religious houses and gifts to Jangams
quote: If he is to be let back he has to pay a certain sum to the different religious houses in the town, gifts to Jangams, and in rare cases he has to give a caste feast.
notes: Fines go to the Liṅgāyat maṭhs; Śaṅkara seats play no part

what_is_said: The 1959 account renames Satyabodh's house the Uttarādi maṭh and says Vyāsatīrtha's branch has devotees scattered in Dharwar; Mādhvas have 'a firm hold' in the district
quote: In his time, the matha which began to be known as Uttaradimatha and subsequently as Satya- bodha-Swamimatha after his name, gained great wealth.
notes: p. 160-61: Mādhva philosophy 'had a firm hold in the district of Dharwar where their population is large'

what_is_said: The Savanur Vaiṣṇav maṭh is described in nearly the 1884 words
quote: The Vaisnava math of Satya- bodhasvami in the heart of the town is a large building in good repairs. A yearly fair in honour of the Svami attended by a large number of his Vaisnava follow’ers is held at the Holi time
notes: Page approximate (Places, Savanur)

what_is_said: A Mādhva pāṭhaśālā (est. 1895) with c. 20 students is funded by donations from the Uttarādi maṭh and the public

notes: Same list names a Shankaracharya Sanskrit Pathashala (est. 1887)

what_is_said: By 1959 the Mūrusāvira maṭh runs a Sanskrit college with free boarding for 75 and helped found a commerce college (1947); the 1884 story is repeated, the Kudalgi lawsuit dropped
quote: It is managed by His Holiness the Swamiji of Murusavira Mafha. A free boarding and lodging house accommodating 75 students is attached to this college.
notes: Hubli maṭhs also listed: Kalyāṇa maṭh, built c. 300 years ago, income c. Rs 800

what_is_said: The Fakīrsvāmī maṭh at Sirahatti, venerated by Liṅgāyats, enjoys an inām of Rs 1,000 a year
quote: The math enjoys an inam of Rs. 1,000 a year. The tomb of Fakirsvaini is highly venerated by the Lihgayats.

what_is_said: Vīraśaiva maṭhs are in all parts of the district; rarely is a village without one
quote: The mathas of the Veerashaivas in particular are found im all parts of the district. Each matha is an independent institution whose head is a guru who is highly venerated.
notes: Edition dated 1966 (the selection lists 1959). Next: 'There is rarely a village in the district which is without a Veerashaiva matha'

what_is_said: The 1966 Places chapter names several Vīraśaiva maṭhs (Chandragiri, Shantaveera with a high school, Sangana Basaveshvara, Ilkal's Virakta maṭh, Mahalingeshvara); none appeared in 1884

notes: Ilkal: 'There is a Veerashaiva Matha,here presided over by a Virakta Swami called Mahantaswami' (p. 508)

what_is_said: Brahmans (mostly Deshasths) are Smārtas following Śaṅkarācārya or Vaiṣṇavas following Madhvācārya; no seat or numbers given
quote: The Brahmins follow two religious faiths—Smartha and the Vaishnava. The Smarthas of Bijapur include a small sect called Kanvashakha
notes: The Sonda/Savanur guru detail of 1884 is gone

what_is_said: The Kaneri maṭh entry repeats 1886, with income now Rs 1,300 and 5,000-6,000 disciples

notes: Income stated slightly lower than 1886 (Rs 1,500)

notes: Hunter's 'Hari' preachers; not a named order.

what_is_said: South-east Maimansinh Hindus mostly Vaishnav, followers of Ram Krishna Gosain, sect headquartered in Sylhet with many akhras; 11,991 Vaishnavs v. 43 Sanyasis.
quote: The Hindu population in the south-eastern part of the District mostly belong to the Vaishnav sect, and pay great venera- tion to the memory of one R4m Krishna Gosdin, who is said to have first introduced Vishnuvite tenets into this part of the country. This sect has its head-quarters in the neighbouring District of Silhet
notes: Page not printed in the OCR.

what_is_said: Most Chasi Kaibarttas follow Vaishnavism with Gosains as gurus.
quote: Oh&sL Eaibarttas in Hooghly have no real endogamous groups, but are merely subdivided territorially into TTttar-RSrhi and Dakhrn-BSrhi (north and south Baih). Most follow Yaish- navism with Gosaina as 6um or spiritual guides.
notes: Who a large cultivating caste follows instead of a Śaṅkara seat.

what_is_said: Vaishnava temple-math (Chaitanya, Brindabanchandra) founded by Satyadev Saraswati; mahants titled Saraswati until the last was dismissed by the Civil Court in 1903.
quote: The math has dehottar property yielding an income of Es. 1,000 a month. The founder of the math was Satyadev Saiaswati } Bisweswar Eai of Qtiptipara, who built the temple of Ohaitanya- dev, was his disciple.
notes: A Vaishnava house under Daśanāmī (Sarasvatī/Daṇḍī) abbots; see RV25 row.

what_is_said: Guptipara math, with Vaishnava deities and a Chaitanya shrine, is run by Dasanamis and subordinate to the Tarakeswar mahant's mandali.
quote: It is curious that while all the deities worshipped in the Guptipara math bear Vaishnava identity, the institution is run by the Dasanamis who belong to the Saiva sect.
notes: Text: 'Tarakeswar being the chief centre of the Dasanamis in the district, the Guptipara math is subordinate to that at Tarakeswar'. Inversion of rivalry: a Śaṅkara-order network holds a Gaudiya shrine.

what_is_said: Radha-Krishna shrine under married hereditary mahants; Bara akhra with subsidiary akhra at Khamarpara.
quote: These abbots are not cehbates but married men, and the succession passes to their hneal descendants as in the case of ordinary Hindus.
notes: Akhra of Chaturdas Babaji; order not named.

what_is_said: Trading castes (Gandhavaniks, Tambulivaniks, Suvarnavaniks) and low castes (Bagdis, Bauris, Kaibartas, Namasudras) adopted Gauriya Vaishnavism.
quote: Gauriya Vaishnavism provided in course of time a great ideological attraction to the economically and socially neglected classes in the fringe of Hindu society. A large numberof Bagdis, Bauris, Barujibis, Kaibartas, Namasudras and others, who had been turning towards Islam, now began to look at this creed
notes: Also lists Sripats (Atpur, Khanakul, Jirat).

what_is_said: The great majority of Kaibarttas are Vaishnavas and respect a Vaishnava more than a Brahman.
quote: By religion the great majority are ‘Vaishnavas ; and it is said that they pay greater respect to a Yaishuava than to a Brahman.

what_is_said: Home of the Gosain who is guru of the Gaura (Gopal) caste throughout Orissa.
quote: It is the home of the Gosain, who is the general guru of the Gaura caste throughout Orissa.
notes: Rasikananda line (not named in text).

what_is_said: Three land-endowed asthals with up-country mahants; one, Bharath Ramanuja Das, chairs the municipality.
quote: The asthdk are monastic and charitable institutions maintained by endowments of land and managed by mahants or abbots. All three have up-country makants, the most influential of whom, Bharath Ramanuja Das, is Chairman of the municipality.
notes: Order inferred from name (Ramanuja Das) and 'up-country'.

what_is_said: Sebaits of amruta-manohi lands pay only a formal sum to the Jagannath mahants.
quote: the sebdits of amruta manoM grants, grants made for the purpose of keeping up the worship of Jagannathat Purl, are accustomed to pay a merely formal sum to the JagannSth mahants, and use the balance to maintain themselves in comfort and luxury.
notes: Puri maths' lands extend into Balasore.

what_is_said: Emar, Dakhinaparsva and Raghavadas richest; Gaudiya: Radhakanta, Gangamata, Kothabhoga; Oriya and Sisu: Utkaliya Vaishnava; Gobardhana and Sankarananda Saiva.
quote: The Vaisnava Mathas belonging to different sampradayas or sub-sects of the cult are numerous at Puri, of which Emar, Dakhinaparsva and Raghavadas are supposed to be the richest. Prominent among the Goudiya Mathas are Radhakanta, Gangamata and Kothabhoga
notes: Gobardhana called 'one of the oldest in Puri' and founded by Adi Sankaracharya.

what_is_said: About 130 mathas listed with sect; by explicit labels Gaudiya/Gauda-Madhva c. 30, Ramanandi/Pancha Ramanandi c. 19, Ramanuj c. 15, Angila (royal) 7; Śaṅkara-line (Adwaita, Dasanami, Dandi) 7.
figures: c. 130 mathas; Gaudiya c. 30; Ramanandi c. 19; Ramanuj c. 15; Advaita/Dasanami c. 7
quote: This account of the Mathas at Puri is based on the information collected from the Office of the Commissioner of Endowments, Orissa; Various Mathas, and the list of Mathas given by Dr- K. C. Mishra in his work, The Cult of Jagannath. The list is not exhaustive.
notes: Tallies are mine from the OCR; 24 'do.' entries could not be assigned because the two columns are misaligned. Sankaracharya/Bhogabardhan is 'do.' under 'Dandi Sannyasi'.

what_is_said: 1951 Orissa Hindu Endowments Act gives the Commissioner power to remove mahants; 1974 Estates Abolition amendment vests endowments in Government.
quote: But being possessed of huge wealth the Mahantas misutilised the trust property and led a life of luxury and vice against which there was much public resentment.
notes: The 1950s-70s change: endowments under state control.

what_is_said: Temple priests were formerly trained and certified at the Sankaracharya matha; now by the Muktimandap.
quote: The priests of the temple used to be trained at the Sankarachayra Matha and only after obtaining a certi¬ ficate from the Matha were eligible to enter into priesthood and perform worship in the temple, but now this function is being performed by the Muktimandap.
notes: Śaṅkara seat's ritual role at Jagannath, beside the Vaishnava maths' sevas (Raghavadas, Oriya, Emar, Uttarparsva).

what_is_said: Emar maintains the Raghunandan Library (1921) and funds a gold medal (1935, Rs 1,700) for Vedanta with Shri Bhashya.
quote: the Guru Raghunandan Ramanuj Das of Emar Matha of Puri Gold Medal Fund was created with a corpus of Rs. 1,700 in the year 1935.
notes: Medal for the Acharya exam 'in Vedanta with Shri Bhashya' — Emar as a Rāmānuja Vedānta patron. Tagged srivaishnava per 1977; 1908 calls Emar Ramat.

what_is_said: Mahant Govind Ramanuj Das of Uttarparsva endowed a scholarship fund with Rs 2,100 in 1934.
quote: In the year 1934, with the donation of Rs. 2,100 made by Mahant Govind Ramanuj Das of the Uttarparsa Matha, Puri, the Baker Schorslahip Fund was created

what_is_said: Important Vaishnava matha with 75 acres; mahant chosen by lot before the deity; devotees tour to spread the cult.
quote: The Matha has 75 acres (30-35 hecatres) of land the produce of which is used for feeding devotees.
notes: Sampradaya not named.

what_is_said: Belur Math, consecrated 1898, headquarters of the Ramakrishna Order from 1 Jan 1899.
quote: stands the Belur Math, the headquarters of the Ramakrishna Mission, which perhaps represents the most potent force in living memory for a religious and cultural regeneration of modern India.
notes: Same volume (p. 126) names Bhotbagan as 'the seat of the Dasanami sect in the district', Tarakeswar their 'principal stronghold'.
